clue.text: Scot's sane, though he's prone to wander

definitions.meaning: a Scot would say someone sane is '...', no being Scots for not
a wanderer with no fixed home, like a herdsman moving with the seasons

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is of sound mind even though he tends to roam about.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is dialect: in Scots 'no' means 'not', so a sane person is 'no mad', which run together gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer without a settled home is exactly what a roaming tribesman is called.

clue.text: Refusal to spoil probationary period

parts.note: no is a refusal
to vitiate is to spoil or impair

explanation.surface: Turning down a chance to ruin someone's trial period at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice's period of trial in a religious order is the time before taking full vows.

clue.text: Mother inserts key material in mantle

indicators.note: inserts says the key letter goes inside the mother word

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A mother puts a key into the material of a mantelpiece or cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mantle' looks like a cloak or fireplace shelf, but it is the Earth's layer beneath the crust.
explanation.definitionFit: The molten rock below the Earth's crust is the substance that wells up as lava.

clue.text: Coach making application

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an old public stagecoach and careful persistent effort.

clue.text: Self-confessed drug-taker's critic

parts.note: points to the English essayist and literary critic who wrote Confessions of an English Opium-Eater about his own laudanum habit

explanation.surface: A reviewer who has openly admitted to using narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas De Quincey published Confessions of an English Opium-Eater (1821) and also wrote much literary criticism, so both halves describe the one man.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist confessed in print to opium addiction and worked as a critic, so the description fits him precisely.

clue.text: Energetic detectives gather a large number up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole is read from bottom to top
gather says the detectives enclose the large number between them

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
many means a large number

explanation.surface: Lively police officers round up a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department; 'gather' puts the big number inside it, and 'up', in a down clue, reverses the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of vigour and drive is forceful and active.

clue.text: Challenges disconcerted esquire

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A flustered gentleman is faced with objections.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge something is to question it, so the plural noun means questions or doubts raised.

clue.text: Try leaving 3 in river

indicators.note: leaving says the word try departs from the hard-work word

parts.note: 3 refers to the answer of 3-down, whose second sense, application, also means industry

explanation.surface: An attempt to quit a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 3-down's meaning, application, which here gives INDUSTRY; take TRY away.
explanation.definitionFit: This great South Asian waterway flows through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Guy, king's only companion

parts.note: a guy is a man, a chap
ER is Edward Rex, King Edward's royal cipher
one means only, as in the one and only

explanation.surface: A man who is a monarch's sole friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person who accompanies a young unmarried woman in society acts as her escort.

clue.text: Fungus as yet staying outside

indicators.note: the word yet stays on the outside, with the word as placed within it

explanation.surface: Mould that has, so far, remained out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: The single-celled organism used in brewing and baking is a type of fungus.

clue.text: Crook given tail, an amateur lawman

indicators.note: crook as a verb means to bend or twist, so the letters of the next two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal is being followed by a self-appointed enforcer of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like the criminal being tailed, but it is the anagram signal working on GIVEN TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-appointed citizen who punishes wrongdoers without legal authority is an unofficial enforcer.

clue.text: Play doctor and nurse endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the nurse word loses its final letter

parts.note: an amah is a nurse or nanny in East and South Asia

explanation.surface: A theatre piece featuring a doctor and a nurse who never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: AMAH, an Asian nursemaid, loses its last letter H to give AMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece for the stage, a theatrical work.

clue.text: Pluck shown by leaders of the women agitating near Greenham

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters, taken from each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: Courage shown by the protesting women of the Greenham Common peace camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenham Common in Berkshire was the site of a long women's peace camp against nuclear missiles in the 1980s. 'Pluck' looks like courage, but it means to sound a string.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucking a string produces a sharp ringing sound, so the noun names what a pluck makes.

clue.text: It controls canvas in the same fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape or make, so the letters of the preceding words are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A piece of equipment that governs a painter's canvas in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests painting, but it means a ship's sails.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat the rope that adjusts the angle of the main sail is what governs that sail.

clue.text: Battle to get back, for instance, Newgate Calendar

parts.note: the Alma was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War

indicators.note: back says the word for being allowed is read in reverse

parts.note: 'get to' in the sense of being allowed to do something means can

explanation.surface: A fight to recover the old register of notorious criminals, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Newgate Calendar was an 18th-century record of crimes from London's Newgate Prison; 'for instance' flags it as one example of the kind of book defined.
explanation.definitionFit: The Newgate Calendar was a yearly-style published register, an example of a calendar-type annual book.

clue.text: Sponge produced at home, in general

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: in says the at-home word goes inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
in means at home

explanation.surface: A sponge cake baked at home, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' looks like 'generally', but 'in' is the insertion and 'general' is LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French shell-shaped cake is a light sponge, famously recalled by Proust.

clue.text: Display and performance cancelled

parts.note: a show is a performance on stage
an event called off is said to be off

explanation.surface: An exhibition and a show that has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to make a boastful exhibition of it.

clue.text: Beyond control in a trick?

definitions.meaning: in card games a trick is formed from cards played out of each player's hand

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a card in a trick has come out of a player's hand, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unmanageable, and literally describes a card played from a hand.

clue.text: Songwriter's supported by child in care

parts.note: Stephen Foster wrote 'Oh! Susanna' and 'Camptown Races'; with the possessive his name gives fosters
on means resting upon, supported by what is under it

explanation.surface: A composer is backed by a youngster in the care of the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' looks like it should give the usual SON, but it belongs to the definition; 'supported' in a down clue means the songwriter's piece sits above.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy brought up by guardians who are not his birth parents is a looked-after youngster.

clue.text: Having no boundaries from spell of bowling? Not so'

parts.note: in cricket a bowler bowls a spell from one end of the pitch, so an end stands for that stint
less means not so much, as in 'less keen' for not so keen

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's spell that never yields a boundary, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundaries' suggests cricket's fours and sixes, but it means limits. In cricket, bowling is done from one end of the pitch or the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without limits goes on forever, infinite in extent.

clue.text: Music from boat on lake? Ecstasy!

parts.note: a skiff is a small light boat
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A joyful tune heard while boating on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIFFLE was a 1950s British craze for folk and jazz played on homemade instruments such as the washboard.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1950s style of folk-jazz played on improvised instruments is a genre of popular music.

clue.text: Shall we first reduce pieces of meat?

indicators.note: first says the reduce word comes before the shall-we word

parts.note: to cut is to reduce, as with prices
let's is the suggestion 'shall we'

explanation.surface: A diner proposes trimming the portions of meat first.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Shall we first reduce' as 'let's, but put cut first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Small slices of lamb or veal chopped from the neck or ribs are a familiar butcher's item.

clue.text: Colt gets thinner, more streamlined

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form
leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: A young horse slims down and becomes sleeker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with less excess is trimmer and tidier, with nothing extra to hamper it.

clue.text: Ceremoniously perform some lines specially written

indicators.note: specially written suggests the words are rewritten in a new order

explanation.surface: Some verses composed for a formal occasion are read out with ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a marriage or rite with due formality is the meaning, as with a wedding.

clue.text: Child features in news programme

indicators.note: features says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A youngster appears on a TV news bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang British term for a young child or offspring.

clue.text: Gathered round an artist

indicators.note: round says the gathered word goes around the word an

parts.note: people who have gathered have met

explanation.surface: People assembled around a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edouard Manet was a French painter, a forerunner of Impressionism.

clue.text: Sweet stuff!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of impatience meaning nonsense, as in 'stuff and nonsense!'

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a soft confectionery and is also an old exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: Established beliefs do for leading scholar in 2

indicators.note: for leading says the word do takes the place of the scholar at the front

parts.note: 2 refers to the answer of 2-down, the molten rock
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fixed doctrines suit a leading academic in the second.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the opening MA of 2-down's answer with DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of principles laid down as incontrovertibly true is a body of doctrine.

clue.text: Government leader's in control, as a rule

indicators.note: in says the leading letter goes inside the control word

parts.note: reins are used to control a horse, so a rein is a check or control

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The head of government holds power as a matter of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of leader's is 'is', linking the pieces: G is inside REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of sovereignty is the time they hold power.

clue.text: Dances, note, and song orchestrated

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: orchestrated means arranged for the orchestra, so the letters of the two words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A list of musical items: dance tunes, a note, and a song scored for an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: These lively Spanish dances in triple time are performed with castanets.

clue.text: Stars as so-called lexicographer

definitions.meaning: Samuel Johnson, compiler of the 1755 Dictionary, was nicknamed Ursa Major for his gruff manner

explanation.walkthrough: Boswell's father dubbed Dr Johnson 'Ursa Major' for his bearish manners; in English that is the constellation's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation's English name was also the nickname given to the dictionary-maker Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Pulled back to the middle? Not I!

indicators.note: back says what remains is read in reverse
not I says the letter I is removed from the centre-ward word

parts.note: moving towards the centre is moving inward

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it was not they who were dragged back to the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: INWARD without its I leaves NWARD, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulled means hauled or dragged, as a cart is by a horse.
